title: FDE Decomposition / Case Study
description: The single biggest filter in FDE loops (~40% pass rate). Practice narrating the 5-step rubric aloud: clarify → stakeholders → inputs → subproblems → walking-skeleton MVP. Every prompt below is drawn from documented Palantir/OpenAI/Anthropic/Turing FDE loops.

questions.prompt: A large city wants to reduce 911 response times using call data, traffic patterns, and ambulance GPS. Design your first 60 minutes with the customer.

rubric.criterion: Clarify: which failure mode matters most (dispatch delay? routing? staging?), current baseline, geographic scope
Stakeholders named: dispatch, EMS ops, city IT, unions, civil-rights review; success metric owner identified
Inputs mapped: freshness of GPS, call taxonomy, traffic feed licensing, PII rules
Decomposed into 2-4 workstreams sequenced by risk/value
Walking-skeleton MVP proposed: e.g. one district, one call type, dashboard-only recommendation before automated dispatch
Names failure modes and rollback (bad recommendation harms response)

questions.modelAnswer: First 10 min: ask which metric moves — average response time, tail P95, or 'response by ZIP equity'. Identify the accountable exec. Next 20 min: map data — GPS refresh interval, call classifier fidelity, city traffic API terms. Next 15 min: decompose into (1) baseline analytics dashboard, (2) staging-location optimizer, (3) real-time dispatch assist. Sequence: (1) first (no risk), then (2) as recommendation, then (3) gated behind human confirmation. Last 15 min: propose 4-week MVP scope = dashboard for one borough, one call category, no automated action.

questions.prompt: A regional bank has 3 recently-acquired fraud-detection systems with inconsistent labels. Scope a 90-day plan to unify.

rubric.criterion: Clarifies: keep all 3 models running or replace? cost of false positives vs negatives? regulatory reporting
Data reconciliation plan: unified label schema, historical relabeling, gold-set curation
Doesn't propose 'one big model' Day 1 — phased approach
Weeks 1-30: shadow + eval; 30-60: pick winner or ensemble; 60-90: cutover with rollback
Compliance & audit story: model risk management doc
Explicit rollback + kill switch per system

questions.modelAnswer: Week 1: interview each fraud team on their taxonomy, get 6 months of labeled data, agree unified label set with regulator input. Weeks 2-6: replay all 3 models on unified holdout; measure precision/recall/economic impact per segment. Weeks 6-10: choose ensemble strategy (union of alerts with a meta-classifier). Weeks 10-12: shadow deployment. Week 12+: cutover behind a per-region flag with immediate rollback path. Deliver an MRM (Model Risk Management) doc for compliance.

questions.prompt: A pharma researcher wants an AI assistant to query internal compound + trial data. Legal, IP, and compliance stakeholders are nervous.

rubric.criterion: Clarifies who is allowed to see which data (compound-level access controls, active trials)
Deployment inside customer VPC only; no third-party API for retrieval or generation
Full audit log with user, query, retrieved docs, response, timestamp
PII / patient data redaction pre-embedding
Read-only assistant to start; escalation to structured tools later
Ethics + IP review board loop before wider rollout

questions.modelAnswer: Scope MVP as a read-only Q&A over public + Phase-completed compound docs. Data classification tags flow into retrieval filters keyed on user role. Self-hosted embedding + LLM in customer VPC. Every query logged to an immutable audit store with user identity and retrieved doc ids. Legal + IP review the retrieval corpus before onboarding. Second phase adds Phase-active data with additional attestation. No autonomous actions in v1.

questions.prompt: A logistics company wants to deploy an AI agent to reroute shipments using SAP data, weather APIs, and 500 warehouse managers as end users.

rubric.criterion: Clarifies: what does 'success' mean — cost, on-time delivery, warehouse manager time saved?
Human-in-the-loop for any action above impact threshold
Phased rollout: shadow → advisory → semi-autonomous → autonomous
Observability + kill-switch per warehouse
Change-management for warehouse managers (training, feedback loop)
Explicit failure modes (bad reroute costs money, upsets customers)

questions.modelAnswer: Start with 5 warehouses in shadow mode: agent produces recommendations, manager sees them but acts as normal. Compare agent decisions vs manager decisions vs outcomes for 30 days. Advance to advisory (manager one-click accept). Then to auto-approve for low-dollar reroutes; escalate high-dollar. Per-warehouse toggle; centralized dashboard on cost saved + errors. Weekly office hours with managers to feed corrections back into the eval set.

questions.prompt: An insurer wants automated summarization of 30M historical claims for adjusters. Regulation varies by state.

rubric.criterion: Clarifies: is the summary attached to the claim (regulated artifact) or an adjuster's tool (advisory)?
Per-state config drives allowed fields, PHI/PII handling, retention
Eval set built with adjusters (what makes a 'good' summary?)
Hallucination guardrails: cite source lines; refuse when uncertain
Rollout: pilot state, then multi-state with per-state review
Feedback loop from adjusters into evaluation

questions.modelAnswer: Advisory tool. Adjuster sees summary alongside raw claim, always. Model prompt requires cited spans; UI shows citations. State-config table drives what fields are allowed to appear. Golden eval set of 200 claims labeled by senior adjusters with 'must-have', 'nice-to-have', 'must-not-have'. Start in one small state; expand only after clean eval + adjuster satisfaction.

questions.prompt: A healthcare client deployed your AI platform 90 days ago. Adoption is 12%. Diagnose + plan.

rubric.criterion: Refuses to jump to 'we need better training' — investigates first
Talks to non-adopters directly; segments them by role/workflow
Analyzes product telemetry: activation funnel, feature usage, drop-off points
Compares heavy users vs light users vs non-users — what's different?
Names 2-3 hypotheses with cheap tests, ranked
Escalation plan if adoption is a workflow/political problem, not a product one

questions.modelAnswer: Week 1: pull activation funnel; interview 5 non-adopters + 5 heavy users. Common hypotheses: (a) workflow doesn't include our tool at the right moment, (b) results aren't trusted, (c) IT policy blocks part of the flow. Rank cheapest test first. Test 1: shadow the current workflow with a heavy user, see where they'd hand off. Test 2: run a trust survey. Week 2: prioritize the biggest gap and ship a 1-week fix. Report to the sponsoring exec with a written 30/60/90-day recovery plan.

questions.prompt: You deployed an AI agent at a bank. Three weeks in, outputs violate undisclosed internal policies.

rubric.criterion: Immediately pauses affected functions rather than debate scope
Gets the actual policies documented in writing
Retroactive audit: which past outputs also violated? Report + remediate
Adds guardrails (policy-check pass) + updated eval set with policy violations as negatives
Post-incident review with client, no blame, focus on process gap
Escalation: contract has SLA — get legal + hiring manager in the loop early

questions.modelAnswer: Hour 0: kill affected function, notify client stakeholders + our leadership. Hour 4: interview client compliance to list every policy that applies. Day 2: retroactive audit — flag any output that likely violated; draft remediation. Day 3-7: build a policy-check gate that runs on every output before delivery; incorporate examples into eval set. Week 2: post-incident with client — process failure was ours (should have asked for policies up front) — propose new intake checklist for future engagements.

questions.prompt: Walk through the 5-step FDE decomposition framework on a NEW problem you've never seen: 'A city wants an AI to spot potholes from streetlight camera footage.'

rubric.criterion: Step 1 clarify: which cameras, what resolution, which departments own the response
Step 2 stakeholders: city IT, DoT, camera-owning agency, residents, unions, budget owner
Step 3 inputs: video access legality, retention, night footage quality, false-positive tolerance
Step 4 decompose: (a) detection, (b) triage/ranking, (c) dispatch workflow integration
Step 5 walking skeleton: 10 cameras, daily batch, dashboard for DoT triage, no dispatch automation v1
Names how to measure success (potholes-fixed-per-dollar; not just detection accuracy)

questions.modelAnswer: See rubric — the point is narrating each step aloud, ending with a scoped 4-week MVP that produces a dashboard reviewed by DoT before any autonomous action.
